data.narrative:
Exowatt, a Series A frontier-tech company in Climate & Energy founded by Hannan Happi and Jack Abraham, has raised $90M to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 same-sector peers—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—though the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with tight valuation clustering.

Given data constraints, Stage-Progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using the $90M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields $180M. This method reflects standard venture progression mechanics but is calibrated only against this single company's funding history rather than peer multiples.

The triangulation range is $153M to $207M, with a median of $180M. This narrow band reflects reliance on one quantitative method; peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or similarly-valued comparables in the Climate & Energy sector. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer multiples, which limits confidence in the stage-progression multiple itself, and the lack of company-specific revenue, unit economics, or technology risk adjustments. Investors should weight this valuation as a stage-based reference point rather than a defensible market consensus.
